t: A handheld tool that lets you talk to chips by typing simple commands.
steps: Buy a Bus Pirate 5 or the newer Bus Pirate 6 from DirtyPCBs, Blinkinlabs or The Pi Hut.
Plug it into your computer with a USB-C cable.
Open a serial terminal app with VT100 colors, or use the browser terminal.
Pick a mode such as I2C from the menu.
Turn on the power supply and set it to 3.3 volts.
Connect a small I2C sensor board with the probe cable.
Run a bus scan and read a value from the sensor.
Update the firmware later by dragging a UF2 file onto the drive.
meta: Wild Open. From $42.50. A few stores.
